item.title: Opening the ConVOI academic year: the Expected Value of Causal Ambiguity
item.description:
I was invited by Anna Heath to open the new academic year of ConVOI, the Collaborative Network for Value of Information, with a talk on Decision-Making under complexity and uncertainty: Causal Ambiguity in Ethnoecology Research.

I presented my work on the Expected Value of Causal Ambiguity: what is at stake when stakeholders work from different causal models of the same system, as with a road decision in a Hmong community in Laos.

The group knows value of information inside out. Within 45 minutes they linked the problem to structural uncertainty analysis, causal discovery, model averaging, multi-criteria decision analysis, Pareto-based value of information and tipping-point analysis. I came away with sharper questions, a clearer view of where the idea sits in existing work, and some promising directions to develop together.

Thank you to everyone who took part for being so generous with your time and so constructively critical. I look forward to continuing the conversation.

item.title: Sino-Europe Young Leadership in Bioeconomy: Mountain Futures Summer School
item.description:
I taught at the Sino-Europe Young Leadership in Bioeconomy: Mountain Futures Summer School in Yunnan, China, from August 12–25, 2026, together with Prof. Jianchu Xu. The summer school was hosted by Mountain Futures and the Landscape Alliance (CIFOR & ICRAF), together with the Chinese Academy of Sciences and a range of supporting partners.

A journalist covered our travels, and the video below gives a good impression of the summer school.

item.title: Uganda 2014: a film of my PhD fieldwork by Rainer Hanke
item.description:
In 2014 Rainer Hanke made a film about my PhD fieldwork in Southwest Uganda, Gardens, Markets and communities with Dr. Katja Kehlenbeck and PhD student Cory Whitney. It follows our work on homegardens, ethnobotany and agroecology with farming communities. The film was never published, and I could not put it on YouTube because of the music. Rainer has since passed away. I am glad to finally share his work, which is now hosted at the Internet Archive.

The film is in German and runs about 44 minutes.

Watch or download the film at the Internet Archive

Video by Rainer Hanke, 2014.
